findings.title: Signature search escapes the inventory block (find_signature scans the whole document)
findings.reason: Mechanism REPRODUCED against HEAD without changing anything: find_signature() (inventory.py:243-260) matches SIGNATURE_LINE on every line of the document, not the [(start,end)] ranges find_blocks() returns; SIGNATURE_LINE allows leading whitespace, so a fenced/indented documentation example outside the block matches. A doc with an unsigned inventory plus the documented example in prose returned the prose line (idx 5, outside block (8,13)); the same doc with a real envelope in the block raised '2 inventory-signature lines — a document carries one signature'. _place_signature() (inventory.py:290-301) has the same reach: it REPLACES an existing envelope line wherever it is, so `sign` on that doc would overwrite the prose example instead of signing the block — the docstring says the envelope 'sits where find_blocks already looks', which is true of placement on a clean doc and false of discovery. run_report.signed_inventory() calls the same find_signature over the whole report text (run_report.py:561), so the run-close gate inherits it. The documented example already exists verbatim in a committed report (docs/reports/u-sig-2/build.md:15) — that file has no inventory heading so it is never checked, but a run report that quotes the format is one paste away. DOWNGRADED from P1: every outcome is FAIL-CLOSED — unsigned+example verifies against the example and is refused on digest mismatch (wrong message, right verdict); signed+example is refused as two — no acceptance path opens and no forged or moved signature verifies, because verify_signature() re-derives the digest from the union of all blocks' entries. It is a false-refusal / wrong-diagnostic robustness defect, not an integrity bypass.
findings.scope: Fix is inside the unit's spec files (inventory.py + tests/test_inventory.py): scope find_signature/_place_signature to the block ranges from find_blocks() (the spec's DESIRED BEHAVIOUR 1 says 'a detached envelope block that find_blocks/parse_entries TOLERATE' — inside the block), add a test with the example in prose (unsigned → 'UNSIGNED'; signed → verifies). Small; no semantic change to the signed/unsigned rules. Batch decision.

findings.title: Retention receipt's offline 'binding' check is under-specified (no algorithm, canonical payload, or trust root)
findings.reason: Confirmed as a gap in what the words promise, not as a deviation from the frozen spec. evidence-manifest.md:110 and the compliance-provenance.md row name three receipt fields (log_index, entry_uuid, signature over inventory_sha256) and say the verifier's offline check is 'its fields binding that digest' and that this 'proves the receipt covers these bytes'. Without a named signing algorithm, canonical signed payload, encoding, and a committed log public key / trust root, an implementer of that check can do only string presence + digest equality — which anyone can type, so it proves the receipt NAMES the digest, not that it covers the bytes; the doc's 'not proven: reachable or trusted' disclaimer does not close that gap because it is the signature that would carry the binding. Both docs already state verify.py TODAY checks presence only (verify.py:1824: non-empty strings when a standard is named) and that the binding check is 'specified here and not yet implemented'. The frozen spec (build-u-sig-2.md, DESIRED BEHAVIOUR 3) enumerated exactly those three fields, said 'spec only', and forbade any network step — the branch implements the spec as frozen; the bot's ask (full receipt schema + trust material) exceeds it.
findings.scope: Out of this unit's frozen spec. Belongs with the already-parked verify.py field-binding check (G1 follow-up): define the receipt schema (Rekor SET: the log's Ed25519/ECDSA key, canonical payload, base64 fields) and where the log's public key is committed. Byte budget matters: runtime/evidence-manifest.md is at the clean-sweep activation-load ceiling (33,997/34,000 tokens; 22,326 bytes after this unit), so a schema cannot live there — docs/compliance-provenance.md or a new docs/ page, with the runtime line pointing at it. Batch decision.
